long_biography.plain_text:
Twice in his career, Jack Lafield saw the equity in companies he had spent years developing disappear. The setbacks did not dislodge him from midstream energy. Trained as a chemical engineer at Texas A&M, he moved through Atlantic Richfield, Delhi Gas Pipeline and Mobil. He then founded Triumph Natural Gas with Apache, advised projects through Avia Energy and became a senior corporate-development executive at Crosstex.

In 2009 Lafield assembled former colleagues and private-equity backing to launch Caiman Energy. The team developed gathering and processing infrastructure for Appalachian shale producers, culminating in a multibillion-dollar sale to Williams in 2012. Months later, he and his partners formed a successor focused on the Utica Shale and helped create Blue Racer Midstream. Lafield later moved from chief executive to chairman, continuing to guide major decisions while supporting engineering scholarships and military-veteran education.
